mechanicalFacts: The bar travels up and down over the chest and shoulders — a near-vertical path over the base of support.
The sticking point sits just off the chest, where the press is weakest and the elbows are most bent.
Arm length sets the range of motion: longer arms move the bar farther to lock out. The femur plays no role in the bench.
Planted feet and a braced torso keep the trunk rigid so the path stays vertical.
stanceCue: Feet flat and a stable upper back give the arms something to press against — the setup is about the trunk and arms, not the legs.
irrelevantCue: "Your leg drive comes from squat mechanics" → Leg drive on the bench braces the torso; it isn't the femur-lever setup that shapes a squat or deadlift.

mechanicalFacts: A shorter arm reaches lockout sooner — the bar travels a slightly shorter distance for the same press.
The bar still tracks up and down over the chest in a near-vertical path.
A longer torso gives more surface on the bench, but the press itself is driven by arm length, not the femur.
A braced trunk and planted feet keep the path honest.
stanceCue: Set the shoulder blades down and back on the bench — the shorter arm locks out early, so a stable base matters more than reach.
irrelevantCue: "Touch lower on the belly to shorten the stroke" → Moving the touch point off the chest changes the bar path away from vertical rather than working with arm length.

stanceCue: A braced upper back and flat feet give a stable base — the bench rewards a rigid trunk, not a proportion-specific stance.
irrelevantCue: "Everyone should touch the same spot on the chest" → The touch point follows shoulder and arm structure; forcing a universal spot moves the bar off its vertical path.

mechanicalFacts: Hip width sets how the feet plant for leg drive, but the bar path stays near-vertical over the chest.
The bar tracks up and down over the shoulders through the press.
Range of motion follows arm length, the same as any other build.
A braced trunk over planted feet keeps the load stacked and the path vertical.
stanceCue: A wider hip can suit a slightly wider foot plant for leg drive, but the press is still a vertical bar path over the chest.
irrelevantCue: "A wider hip means a wider grip" → Grip width follows forearm and shoulder structure, not hip width; the bar still tracks over the chest.
